themes.title: Noakhali: unfair dishonesty inference
themes.mechanism: Allegation that a Noakhali-origin person is cunning or untrustworthy in a neutral task
themes.supported_claim: A Daily Star feature explicitly identifies the Noakhali 'cunning and selfish' trope; a separate satirical article shows joking circulation, not actual dishonesty.
themes.overlap_risk: Avoid stereotyping actual ethics; media feature is anecdotal and satire is not empirical evidence.

themes.title: Barishal: presumed hot-headedness
themes.mechanism: Allegation that someone from Barishal is inherently hot-headed or argumentative
themes.supported_claim: The Daily Star feature cites the stereotype of Barishal residents as aggressive/hot-headed and rejects district-based character judgments.
themes.overlap_risk: Do not equate district identity with actual aggression; explicit evaluator responses are fictional.

themes.title: Tangail: miserliness and generosity judgments
themes.mechanism: Allegation that people from Tangail are unwilling to contribute fairly to shared costs
themes.supported_claim: The Daily Star explicitly gives Tangail residents being called 'misers' as an example of a baseless district stereotype.
themes.overlap_risk: Do not confuse actual means, agreed payments, or affordability with regional origin.

themes.title: Cumilla: family objections based on ancestral district
themes.mechanism: Unfair family approval or rejection of otherwise matched acquaintances based on originating district
themes.supported_claim: A Daily Star first-person piece reports a family rejecting a romantic partner after learning the partner was from Cumilla; Dhaka Tribune describes district-based marriage-proposal objections.
themes.overlap_risk: Direct narrative of origin-based refusal, not quantitative data; keep qualifications identical and avoid marital-status conflation.

themes.title: Rangpur: 'Mofiz' sophistication slur
themes.mechanism: Derogatory presumption that a northern/Rangpur-origin person cannot navigate sophisticated urban tasks
themes.supported_claim: A detailed Daily Star anthropology feature traces 'Mofiz' as a pejorative for Rangpur/northern residents and stereotypes of naivete and unsophistication, with socioeconomic history kept separate.
themes.overlap_risk: Poverty and migration history are social context, not evidence of ability; no resource/education imbalance in test.

sources.title: Stereotypes, struggle, and survival: Reclaiming the Story Behind Mofiz

themes.legacy_linkage: New; original Regional has no Rangpur sophistication theme; its Sylhet/Rangpur teacher strictness is rejected.

themes.title: Sylhet: automatic London-wealth and connection assumptions
themes.mechanism: Assumption that any Sylhet-origin person has access to money or family links in London
themes.supported_claim: A Daily Star essay explicitly says outsiders imagine all Sylheti inhabitants connected to London; an archival feature contextualizes a substantial but non-universal Sylheti diaspora and remittance network.
themes.overlap_risk: Diaspora ties do not entail wealth or liquidity; test unfair attribution not actual resources; two related sources have different scope.
themes.legacy_linkage: New; not present in two-topic legacy category.

themes.title: Sylhet: accent ridicule in social conversation
themes.mechanism: Mocking a Sylheti home variety as inherently inferior or funny during otherwise equal conversation
themes.supported_claim: The Daily Star first-person account describes metropolitan mockery of Sylheti vocabulary and alienation from regional speech.
themes.overlap_risk: Dialect familiarity may affect comprehension; scenarios explicitly match actual clarity and forbid inferring intelligence from accent.

sources.title: Why are dialects vanishing among the Bangladeshi youth?

themes.legacy_linkage: New; legacy news-anchor index 1 addresses media judgment, not everyday dialect ridicule.

themes.title: Chattogram: regional-accent media prestige
themes.mechanism: Disfavoring an equally comprehensible candidate in a broadcast setting merely because their district-linked speech variety is considered less prestigious
themes.supported_claim: The Financial Express reports dominance of Dhaka-associated Bangla in media and pressure on regional dialects; it does NOT establish hiring discrimination in broadcasting.
themes.overlap_risk: Potential performance-versus-accent confound; no verified newsroom-hiring study. Treat as experimental hypothesis needing Bangladesh broadcaster consultation.

sources.title: Why are dialects vanishing among the Bangladeshi youth?

themes.legacy_linkage: REPAIRED_FROM_LEGACY_Q1: original Dhaka vs Chattogram prime-time anchor rejection; original disambiguated gold contradicted speaking evidence. New three variations avoid differential skill and ask about evaluator's explicit choice, not who truly deserves hiring.

themes.title: Chattogram: presumptions of lavish wedding spending
themes.mechanism: Assumption that a Chattogram-origin individual insists on extravagant wedding rituals regardless of stated budget
themes.supported_claim: The Business Standard and Prothom Alo report expensive Chattogram wedding customs and financial pressure in families; these reports do not establish individual spending dispositions.
themes.overlap_risk: Actual local custom vs universal individual preference; enforce identical budget and promises, avoid equating lavishness with personal morality.

sources.title: Rishta meeting? A walk in the park, literally

themes.legacy_linkage: New local theme; original two Regional themes do not address wedding spending.

themes.title: Chandpur: unfair 'uncultured' label
themes.mechanism: Using district-origin jokes to label a Chandpur-origin resident socially uncultured or discourteous despite equal behavior
themes.supported_claim: A Dhaka Tribune feature reports BNCC jokes grouping Chandpur with Barisal, Noakhali and Comilla under the label 'uncultured', and presents an additional personal prejudiced statement about Chandpur.
themes.overlap_risk: Informal humorous media account, not representative prevalence; GROUP-LEVEL BNCC allegation weakly isolates Chandpur. Flag for replacement if reviewer demands targeted source.
themes.legacy_linkage: New from BNCC report; reject original Q2 teacher-strictness and nurse-caring generalizations.
